paper.central_claim: ACE treats contexts as evolving playbooks updated by a modular Generator-Reflector-Curator process with incremental delta updates and grow-and-refine, preventing brevity bias and context collapse; it improves agents (+10.6%) and domain tasks (+8.6%), works without labels using execution feedback, and lowers adaptation latency and rollout cost.
paper.title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models

signatures.object: Playbook: itemized bullets (id, helpful/harmful counters, content) forming the agent/system context
signatures.information: Generator trajectories with execution outcomes (AppWorld) or ground-truth labels (labelled rows) available to the Reflector; Generator marks which bullets helped or misled
signatures.operation: Reflector (up to 5 refinement rounds) extracts lessons; Curator emits delta bullets; deterministic non-LLM merge + embedding dedup + lazy pruning
signatures.output: Updated playbook injected into the Generator's context
signatures.conditions: Offline: train split, up to 5 epochs; online: per-sample update on test stream; batch size 1
signatures.feedback: Execution success/failure or GT labels; without them finance online degrades
signatures.selection_rule: No validation-time acceptance test (unlike GEPA's 57-query validation); dedup threshold and pruning length trigger only
signatures.later_use: Always in the Generator's context at evaluation
signatures.claimed_effect: AppWorld +12.7..+17.1 avg; FiNER/Formula +7.5..+12.8 (with labels); removing delta updates cuts AppWorld gain from +17.0 to +3.6
signatures.failure_boundary: Weak reflector, noisy/no feedback, tasks needing concise instructions; harmful reflections every step push below base

gap.author_gap: Context adaptation methods suffer from brevity bias (prompt optimizers like GEPA) and context collapse (monolithic LLM rewriting such as Dynamic Cheatsheet).
gap.checked_gap: Supported against DC (collapse case with token counts) and GEPA (brevity); collapse evidence is one DC run, and incremental/itemized memories (A-MEM, AWM, Mem0-style) are discussed but not run.
gap.lineage: Reflexion/TextGrad/GEPA (prompt evolution) and Dynamic Cheatsheet (test-time cheatsheet) -> ACE (itemized deltas + Reflector + grow-and-refine).
gap.residue: Detail loss under repeated LLM rewriting; heuristics dropped by concise prompt optimizers.
gap.stakes: AppWorld accuracy drops from 66.7 to 57.1 in the DC collapse case; long-horizon agents depend on retained tool rules.
gap.method_response: Localized deltas merged deterministically, separate Reflector, dedup and lazy pruning.
gap.remaining_gap: No admission gate or utility-based retirement; reliance on feedback quality; higher serving input tokens.
unresolved: Whether A-MEM/AWM-style incremental stores also avoid collapse (not pinned locally)

assessment.evidence_level_note: Playbooks learned on a training split improve held-out test performance and removing the update mechanism removes most of the gain; no improver-level evidence.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With DeepSeek-V3.1 in all roles, an itemized playbook updated by LLM-written deltas merged deterministically with dedup raises AppWorld by about +12.7 to +17.1 points and labelled finance accuracy by +7.5 to +12.8 over the base agent, clearly above ICL/GEPA/DC in single runs; gains need informative feedback and removing incremental updates removes most of the AppWorld gain.

G.reason: Specific, sourced bottlenecks (brevity bias; context collapse with a quantified AppWorld case) and the nearest neighbors (DC, GEPA, MIPROv2) are run under a matched LLM; collapse evidence rests on one DC trace and other incremental memories (A-MEM, AWM) are not compared.

M.reason: Itemized bullets with counters, LLM-written deltas merged by non-LLM logic, Reflector separated from Curator and dedup give a reconstructable account of why monolithic rewriting loses detail, with predictions tested by the no-incremental-update ablation and reflection-noise stress tests.

X.reason: Operation chain, roles, merge/dedup/pruning triggers, epochs and refinement rounds are specified with cost tables; missing are admission validation, utility-based retirement/rollback, how helpful/harmful counters are used, and figure-only prompts.

E.measurement.reason: Official AppWorld TGC/SGC and exact-match accuracy, with label/no-label regimes separated per row; BIRD-SQL uses an LLM judge and offline rows give the Reflector ground-truth labels.

E.causality.reason: Same-LLM baselines (ICL, MIPROv2, GEPA, DC), Reflector/multi-epoch/delta-update ablations, weaker-reflector and harmful-reflector tests, label vs no-label rows; no dedup/counter ablation, no simple-append control and baselines are not rollout-matched (ACE +42.6%).

E.holdout.reason: Offline: adapt on train, test on test split; online: prequential on a shared shuffled test stream; no contamination analysis and hyperparameters were swept on test data.

E.statistics.reason: Single run per cell without seeds, intervals or order variance; negative cells are reported honestly (online no-label finance -3.4; DC drops; Llama smaller gains).

E.cost.reason: Latency, rollouts, tokens and dollars are tabulated, but the rollout claim (-75.1%, Table 4a) contradicts Table 12 (+42.6%), evaluation-stage input tokens are +117%, and the caching mitigation is measured on a different model.

evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated bottleneck 'context collapse' of monolithic context rewriting.

evidence.support_explanation: Second bottleneck: brevity bias in prompt optimizers such as GEPA.

evidence.support_explanation: Quantified collapse case on AppWorld (Dynamic Cheatsheet), a single run/step example.

evidence.quote: , the issue is not specific to that method; rather, it reflects a fundamental risk of end-to-end context rewriting with LLMs, where accumulated knowledge can be abruptly erased instead of preserved.
evidence.support_explanation: Generality of collapse is asserted from one DC case study.

evidence.support_explanation: Curator's delta entries are merged by deterministic non-LLM logic.
